Hi all — thanks for the context. A few notes from Legal on sequencing and turnaround so ACME can plan:

Recommended sequencing (Redwood Legal POV):
1) NDA (mutual, limited) — get this signed first so security can receive sample data and complete the questionnaire. We can usually turn around standard NDA redlines in 2–3 business days. If ACME has significant custom clauses it may be longer.
2) DPA — prepare a draft DPA to share with ACME legal in parallel. DPA comments are frequently scoped and take ~7–10 business days to agree. If EU residency is required, we’ll include the appropriate annex.
3) MSA — MSA negotiation is usually the longest; expect 10–14 business days for the first negotiation cycle. We recommend receiving ACME’s redlines in a single tracked Word doc to avoid mismatched versions.

Redline and signature process:
- We accept Word redlines for MSA and DPA negotiations.
- For NDA, either DocuSign (preferred for speed) or countersigned PDF is fine.
- Please include a consolidated set of redlines; our Legal team will not respond to multiple parallel redline streams.

Data residency / security notes:
- Redwood offers US-only residency by default. EU residency is available with an add-on and requires a short implementation lead time (we’ll put specific dates in the DPA appendix).
- If ACME requires on-prem or air-gapped options, that’s an enterprise conversation but would be additional procurement/engineering effort.

Deliverables we’ll produce once contacts are confirmed:
- Final Redwood NDA (DocuSign-ready)
- Draft DPA (with US residency default; EU variant if requested)
- Example SOW template and timing estimates for pilot and production phases

Alex / Susan — can you confirm: 1) who will circulate ACME’s redlines (legal@acme.com or procurement@acme.com), and 2) whether ACME prefers DocuSign for the NDA?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
